chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-Askari narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Bazzaz narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Abul-Rabi' Suleiman ibn Dawud narrated to us, saying: Faraj ibn Fudalah, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyah, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

When my nation practices fifteen characteristics, the calamity is averted (or: becomes inevitable/dissolved), it was said: O Messenger of God, what are they? He said: When the war booty is distributed among factions (or: becomes a source of envy/strife), and trustworthiness becomes a gain (or: is treated as profit), and alms-tax becomes a loss (or: is considered a burden), and a man obeys his wife but disobeys his mother, and is kind to his friend but neglects his father, and the leader of the people is the worst of them, yet the people honor him out of fear of his evil, and voices rise in the mosques, and they wear silk, and they take singers and play instruments, and the latter of this nation curse the former, then let him await the red wind, or the swallowing up (earthquake), or the transformation (of humans into animals).

key_terms.الدُّوَلُ: Factions or groups (implying distribution among elites or envy)
key_terms.الرِّيحَ الْحَمْرَاءَ: The red wind (a specific eschatological sign)
key_terms.الْمَغَانِمُ: War booty or spoils of war

ai.seo_question: What are the fifteen signs that indicate the approach of calamities in the Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a diagnostic tool for societal decay, where the inversion of core virtues—such as treating trust as profit and charity as loss—precipitates divine punishment. The narration highlights specific eschatological markers, including the rise of the unworthy to leadership and the proliferation of luxury, which signal the imminent arrival of calamities like the red wind or transformation. This serves as a warning that moral corruption at the communal level directly triggers cosmic retribution.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 15-1 Al-Hassan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa’id al-Askari narrated that Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Baz’zaz quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Ar’tar, on the authority of Abul-Rabi’a Suleiman ibn Davood, on the authority of Faraj ibn Fuzalat, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafyat, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “My nation may experience serious trouble if they practice fifteen things.” He (MGB) was asked, “O Prophet of God! What are these things?”

He (MGB) replied, “They are the following: the nation’s capital is controlled by a few special people; people do not honor what they are entrusted with; people consider the payment of the alms-tax as a form of loss; men obey their wives but they disobey their mothers; people are kind to their friends but they hurt their fathers; the worst people in the society run the affairs of the people and the best of the people fear the one who runs the affairs and his wicked deeds; the mosques get filled with loud (forbidden) sounds; people wear silk clothes; people play musical instruments and hire singers; the latter people in the nation curse the former ones. In this situation you can expect red winds, landslides , and drastic changes in the people.
